pages.text: Modules tell a drone $(l)what job to do$(). Install them in the $(l:drone_systems/drone_assembler)Drone Assembler$(/l), together with a $(l:drone_systems/drone_frames)frame$(/l).

A drone with more than one module $(l)takes turns$(): after each trip back to the dock it tries the next module first, so no job is forgotten. You can see the installed modules on the drone itself: each one adds its own tool on it, and those under the hull share the space from front to back.

Every module makes the drone use more power in flight, and some jobs cost energy too:$(br)$(li)$(l)Harvester Module$(): +1 FE/t, 40 FE per harvest$(br)$(li)$(l)Quarry Module$(): +2 FE/t, 20 FE + 10 FE per point of hardness, per block$(br)$(li)$(l)Transport Module$(): +1 FE/t, none
pages.title: Power use

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Planter Module$(): +1 FE/t, 10 FE per seed$(br)$(li)$(l)Logger Module$(): +2 FE/t, 20 FE per log, 5 FE per leaf block$(br)$(li)$(l)Taxi Module$(): +2 FE/t, 50 FE per trip$(br)$(li)$(l)Rancher Module$(): +1 FE/t, 15 FE per shearing or milking$(br)$(li)$(l)Fertilizer Module$(): +1 FE/t, 10 FE per use

$(li)$(l)Builder Module$(): +2 FE/t, 20 FE per block$(br)$(li)$(l)Fisher Module$(): +1 FE/t, 10 FE per catch$(br)$(li)$(l)Breeder Module$(): +1 FE/t, 15 FE per animal fed$(br)$(li)$(l)Guard Module$(): +2 FE/t, 150 FE per shot$(br)$(li)$(l)Bomb Module$(): +1 FE/t, the Mini Drone itself

The drone looks for $(l)fully grown crops$() in its work area, harvests them and $(l)replants$() them, using one of the dropped seeds if there is one. It also harvests $(l)melons and pumpkins$(), and $(l)picks$() ripe plants that give their fruit to a right-click, like sweet berry bushes, leaving the plant in place.
Works with wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot and modded crops and bushes built like the vanilla ones. A $(l:drone_systems/addons)Fortune Addon$(/l) gives more crops and seeds.

pages.title: Quarry Module
pages.text: The drone $(l)digs out the work area layer by layer$(), from the top of the area all the way down to bedrock. The dock GUI shows the layer it is working on.

$(li)It digs $(l)in order$(): row by row along the layer, zig-zagging, and every other layer it walks back the other way, so it never has to fly across the pit.$(br)$(li)It flies back to unload after $(l)192 items$() (three stacks).

$(li)It $(l)only works with a surveyed area$(): the default area around the dock is never dug, so your base is safe. Mark the area with the $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Survey Tool$(/l).$(br)$(li)Blocks drop as if mined with a $(l)diamond pickaxe$(). Add Fortune or Silk Touch with $(l:drone_systems/addons)addons$(/l).

$(li)It skips $(l)liquids$(), $(l)unbreakable blocks$() and anything with an inventory or a machine inside (chests, furnaces, CyberFarm machines).$(br)$(li)The column right under the Drone Dock is never dug, so the dock stays on a pillar.

$(li)In a deep pit it climbs out over the rim and drops straight down the shaft, so the dock can sit beside the pit. A layer is finished only when every block in it is dug: a block the drone could not reach is tried again on the next trip, never skipped.

$(li)The $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)dock filter$(/l) decides which drops are $(l)kept$(); the others are thrown away.$(br)$(li)Harder blocks take longer and cost more power: about 25 FE for dirt, 35 FE for stone, 520 FE for obsidian.

The drone carries items $(l)from one container to another$(): it picks up a load at the $(l)source$(), flies to the $(l)destination$() and empties it there. It keeps going while the source has items and the destination has room.

A load is $(l)16 items$(); each $(l:drone_systems/addons)Stack Addon$(/l) adds a full stack (64 items), up to 9 stacks. While loaded, the drone carries the item $(l)in its claw$(), so you can see what it is moving.

Both containers must be within $(l)48 blocks of the dock$(), in loaded chunks. If something stands in the way, the drone climbs over it; if it stays stuck for 5 seconds it gives that container up and goes home until its next trip.$(br2)Set the route with the $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Survey Tool$(/l) in $(l)Route$() mode: click the source

container, then the destination. Any inventory works, including ones from other mods and $(l)other drones' docks$(): a Transport drone can collect what a Harvester or a Quarry brings home. Items that do not fit in the destination are brought back to the dock. The $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)dock filter$(/l) decides $(l)which items$() are moved.

pages.title: Planter Module
pages.text: The drone plants seeds on $(l)empty farmland$() in its work area. It loads up to a stack of seeds $(l)from its dock$() before each trip, so it works perfectly with a Harvester: harvested seeds go to the dock and the Planter puts

them back in the ground. You can also fill the dock with a hopper. Its tank feeds a pump under the hull, which sprays green on each block it sows.$(br)$(li)Plants anything that grows on farmland: wheat seeds, carrots, potatoes, beetroot seeds, melon and pumpkin seeds, and modded crops.
$(li)It $(l)never tills soil$(): hoe the field once and it will keep it planted.$(br)$(li)Seeds it did not use go back to the dock.

The drone finds the $(l)trees$() in its work area (a log standing on soil), parks next to the trunk and fells the whole tree $(l)from the top down$(), leaves included, so it also collects saplings and apples. Then it $(l)replants a sapling$() where the trunk stood.

$(li)Works with every vanilla tree and with modded trees using the standard log and leaf tags.$(br)$(li)Leaves you placed yourself are never touched.$(br)$(li)Fortune gives more saplings and apples; Silk Touch collects the leaf blocks themselves.
$(li)A big tree can drop more than the 9 cargo slots hold: the rest falls on the ground.

A personal air taxi. The drone $(l)waits above its dock$() with a cable and a hook. $(l)Right-click it$() to grab the hook: you hang below it with one hand while it carries you to the dock's $(l)taxi destination$(), then it flies home by itself.

$(li)With the $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Survey Tool$(/l) linked to the dock and in $(l)Taxi$() mode, $(l)right-click the block$() you want to land on (up to 256 blocks from the dock, with two blocks of air above it).$(br)$(li)Right-click the waiting drone.

$(li)It climbs above the terrain, flies straight to the destination and puts you down gently.$(br)$(li)Trips are $(l)one way$(): put a second dock with its own Taxi drone at the destination to fly back.$(br)$(li)Before taking off the drone checks it has enough charge for the trip and the way back.
$(li)$(l)Sneak$() to let go mid-flight: you get $(l)Slow Falling$(), so you land safely.$(br)$(li)Speed Addons make the trip faster.

pages.title: Rancher Module
pages.text: The drone looks after the animals in its work area: it $(l)shears$() every sheep (and mooshroom, and any shearable mob from other mods) and $(l)milks$() cows and goats. Wool, milk and the rest go back to the dock.

$(li)Milking needs $(l)empty buckets$(): put them in the dock, the drone takes up to 16 per trip and brings back the milk buckets.$(br)$(li)It chases the animal and hovers just above it, so fence the herd inside the work area.$(br)$(li)Sheep are sheared again once their wool grows back.

pages.title: Fertilizer Module
pages.text: The drone $(l)grows the crops, stems and saplings$() of its work area with fertilizer from the dock, until they are fully grown. It works with $(l)any fertilizer$(): bone meal, Biomass (weak: it grows the plant one time in

three), or fertilizers from other mods (everything in the forge:fertilizers tag). The white canister on its shoulder feeds a pump under the hull, which sprays each plant.$(br)$(li)Put the fertilizer in the dock: the drone takes up to 64 per trip.

$(li)Grass and moss are left alone, so your lawn does not fill with flowers.$(br)$(li)A fertilizer that does not work on a plant is not wasted: the drone skips that plant.$(br)$(li)Pairs well with a Harvester and a Planter on the same field.

The drone $(l)builds a multiblock or a schematic$() for you: the one you lock with the $(l:basics/multiblock_projector)Multiblock Projector$(/l) and link to its dock. It fits $(l)only a$() $(l:drone_systems/drone_frames)Mini Drone Frame$(/l): building is work for a swarm of Mini Drones on a $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Builder Swarm Dock$(/l).

$(li)Pick the structure in the projector's list, $(l)sneak + right-click$() a block to lock it there, then $(l)right-click the dock$() with the projector to link it. Right-click the dock with an unlocked projector to unlink it.

$(li)Put the blocks in the dock: the drone takes one kind per trip, carrying them in its claw.$(br)$(li)First it $(l)clears the site$(), from the top down: it cuts away wrong blocks where the structure goes and anything in a space that must stay empty, and in a schematic's box (above its bottom layer) the ground,

$(li)rocks, trees and plants. What it cuts drops where the block was. It leaves chests, machines and anything else holding things, fluids and unbreakable blocks: the dock screen counts them, and you move them.

$(li)Then it builds $(l)one layer at a time$(), from the bottom: a layer is finished before the next one starts. If the dock runs out of a block the current layer needs, the drone $(l)waits$() for it.

$(li)Each block is $(l)printed$() into place: a shell of light closes in on it and a scan line runs down it. The dock's $(l)Build$() tab shows the layer and the blocks it still needs; the ones the dock has none of are marked in red.
$(li)It flies above the layer it is building, straight from block to block, and goes over the whole structure when something is in the way, so it never gets walled in.
$(li)The dock $(l)takes in only the blocks the build still needs$(). Point a Transport drone's route from your storage to the dock and it brings exactly what is missing, and nothing else.

$(li)Or put $(l)chests next to the dock$(): every second it takes from them what the layer being built still needs, and puts back there what that layer does not use, so its nine slots never fill up with blocks for later layers.
$(li)Doors and beds go in whole. Blocks it cannot place (water, a lantern hanging under a ceiling) are listed in the Build tab at the end, for you to place by hand. Chests go in empty.
$(li)Several Builder drones on different docks can share one build: link the same projection to each dock and they split the blocks between them.

pages.title: Fisher Module
pages.text: The drone $(l)fishes$() in the water of its work area and brings the catch to the dock.$(br)$(li)It needs $(l)open water$(): a water source block with air above it, inside the work area.

$(li)It hovers over the water, waits for a bite like a fishing rod and pulls out what a rod would, with the same odds: mostly fish, some junk and now and then $(l)treasure$() (enchanted books, saddles, name tags...).$(br)$(li)It flies home when its cargo is full.

pages.title: Breeder Module
pages.text: The drone $(l)feeds the animals$() of its work area so they breed, with their food from the dock. A hay rack hangs under its hull, and feed falls from it on each animal it feeds.

$(li)Put the food in the dock: wheat for cows and sheep, seeds for chickens, carrots for pigs, or whatever a modded animal eats. The drone takes the right food for each animal.$(br)$(li)It feeds an animal only when $(l)two of a kind$() are ready, so none of the food is wasted.
$(li)It stops once there are $(l)16 of a kind$() in the work area, babies included, so the farm does not grow without end. Pairs well with a Rancher, or a Harvester for the crops they eat.

pages.title: Guard Module
pages.text: The drone $(l)defends its work area$(): it hunts every hostile mob there and shoots it with the laser on its shoulder, then goes after the next one.

$(li)It looks over the work area and $(l)8 blocks above and below$() it, so it also catches flying mobs and what comes out of a cave. Without a surveyed area that is the default 9x9 square round the dock; mark a bigger one (up to 33x33) with the $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Survey Tool$(/l).

$(li)It hovers $(l)3 blocks over the mob's head$(), out of reach of swords and claws, and fires once a second: $(l)6 damage a shot$(), 150 FE (every CyberFarm laser costs 25 FE per point of damage). Nothing can hurt the drone, creepers included.

$(li)It shoots $(l)hostile mobs only$(), just like the $(l:basics/laser_turret)Laser Turret$(/l): never players, animals, villagers, golems, named mobs, mobs riding something or neutral mobs that are not angry.$(br)$(li)With nothing left to shoot it flies home to charge, and checks again every two seconds.
$(li)Pairs well with any farm module on the same drone, or on its own on a dock by the village gate.

pages.title: Bomb Module
pages.text: A kamikaze drone. It fits $(l)only a$() $(l:drone_systems/drone_frames)Mini Drone Frame$(/l): the Mini Drone waits on its $(l:drone_systems/drone_dock)Builder Swarm Dock$(/l) until a hostile mob comes into the work area, then $(l)dives at it and explodes$().

$(li)It looks over the work area and $(l)8 blocks above and below$() it, and goes for the same mobs as the Guard Module above: never animals, villagers, golems, named mobs or calm neutral mobs.$(br)$(li)With the fuse lit (you hear it hiss) it flies straight at the mob and goes off once it is close.

$(li)The blast is $(l)a small TNT$(), half as strong, going off at the mob's feet: about $(l)24 damage$(), enough for a zombie, a skeleton or a creeper. It $(l)breaks a few blocks$() and hurts anything near it, $(l)players included$(). Keep the work area away from what you built.

$(li)$(l)The drone is used up$(): assemble a new Mini Drone and put it back on the dock. Its place on the pad is free as soon as it goes off.$(br)$(li)Up to four Mini Drones share a Builder Swarm Dock, and $(l)each goes for a different mob$(), so a swarm takes out a whole group.
